channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Ebola en RDC, une épidémie hors de contrôle ?
item.description: Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Frédéric Manantsoa Lai, coordinateur des urgences pour Médecins Sans Frontières, et Onesphore Sematumba, analyste senior pour la République démocratique du Congo et le Burundi à Crisis Group, pour parler de l’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC et de ses conséquences sur la population congolaise, déjà marquée par des années de conflit.

item.title: Avrupa Birliği ve Türkiye: Savunmada Birlik?
item.description: İkinci Dünya Savaşı sonrasında şekillenen uluslararası düzen giderek çözülürken, Ankara ve diğer Avrupa başkentlerindeki yetkililer güvenlik alanında birlikte hareket etmedikleri takdirde ciddi risklerle karşı karşıya kalacaklarının giderek daha fazla farkına varıyor. Tehdit algıları farklılık gösterse de, pragmatik ve esnek iş birliği yolları geliştirmeleri hâlâ mümkün. Avrupa Birliği ve Türkiye: Savunmada Birlik?

item.title: Can Democrats seize on how much everyone hates Trump’s Iran war?
item.description: Amidst the tragifarce of President Donald Trump’s apparently off-the-top-of-his-head war on Iran may lie a silver lining for the 2028 presidential election. a silver lining that comes with two big ifs. One, of course, is the if that goes with everything involved with the race: If there is a fair election.

item.title: Trump says he believes Iranian leader Mojtaba Khamenei still alive
item.description: Officially, Mr. Khamenei continues to lead his country under U. S. and Israeli attack. However, his public absence and the rise to power of veteran Revolutionary Guards figures has fuelled speculation that he is either dead or not fully in command Trump says he believes Iranian leader Mojtaba Khamenei still alive.

item.title: Indonesia’s green transition has a glaring social blind spot
item.description: There is a harsh paradox in today’s sustainability debate. The tools for understanding environmental risk are becoming more sophisticated: financed emissions, climate-risk models, taxonomies, transition plans and carbon pricing are increasingly part of the language of business and finance. This is all important progress. But as the conversation becomes more technical, one question is still [] The Indonesia’s green transition has a glaring social blind spot.

item.title: Former Malaysian PM Ismail Sabri charged with concealing assets
item.description: The anti-graft agency in March last year said Ismail Sabri had submitted an assets declaration after being ordered to do so as part of its investigation into alleged graft and money laundering, following the seizure ‌of nearly $40 million in assets allegedly linked to him. Former Malaysian PM Ismail Sabri charged with concealing assets.

item.title: US transshipment claims in Southeast Asia rest on thin data
item.description: Washington’s August 13 report, The Great Transshipment Scam, puts Southeast Asia at the center of a widening US campaign against tariff evasion worldwide. Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam are all placed in the report’s Tier 2, a category the White House says combines significant transshipment volumes with deep integration into China-linked supply chains.

item.title: Glacial collapse caused seismic activity, ‘catastrophic’ Nepal floods: USGS
item.description: “Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred,” U. S. Geological Survey said. Glacial collapse caused seismic activity, ‘catastrophic’ Nepal floods: USGS.

item.title: Western disturbance linked to Nepal floods
item.description: The western disturbance is a possible contributor to the broader rainfall environment rather than an established direct cause of the flash flood; the immediate mechanism behind the sudden release of water remains under investigation, a senior IMD official says Western disturbance linked to Nepal floods.

item.title: Recent museum thefts in Europe
item.description: Unlike robberies in banks or other institutions that notoriously become violent and traumatic, law enforcement agencies and popular culture have long associated museum thefts with the same ‘elegance’ and sophistication that the targets are known for Recent museum thefts in Europe.

item.title: Life-Saving Resource Or Political Weapon?
item.description: The Ibar River feeds Lake Gazivode, providing drinking water as well as water for crop irrigation and cooling power plants across Kosovo. But after recent local disputes, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has raised the prospect of altering the river's course upstream. Life-Saving Resource Or Political Weapon?

item.title: More health workers, stronger systems: Africa’s new ambitious goal
item.description: Facing a projected shortage of more than six million health professionals by 2035, African countries are stepping up efforts to strengthen their workforce, with a new decade-long plan announced on Wednesday during a meeting of health ministers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. More health workers, stronger systems: Africa’s new ambitious goal.

item.title: US faces surging toilet paper prices amid trade war with Canada
item.description: Paper products among hardest-hit sectors after trade negotiations broke down, with 25-50% tariffs estimatedAre you a Canadian boycotting US products? We’d like to hear from youUsing the bathroom or having a cry is about to become more expensive for North Americans as the US and Canada enter a full-fledged trade war that threatens to flush away decades of peaceful trading between the two nations.

item.title: S Korea’s AI economy can’t compete with China through conformity
item.description: South Korea is betting extraordinary sums on artificial intelligence. President Lee Jae-myung has backed an 800 trillion won (US$578 billion) semiconductor expansion involving Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, promoted a new chip hub in the country’s southwest and joined Korean and US technology companies in AI initiatives valued at hundreds of billions of dollars. item.title: India-France eye a mutually convenient next-gen fighter deal
item.description: India’s interest in joining the French-led Future Combat Air System (FCAS) program reflects a convergence of strategic necessity, where India needs a credible path to next-generation airpower, while France needs a financially and industrially viable partner to sustain its sixth-generation fighter ambitions. This month, India formally began exploring participation in FCAS, according to disclosures India-France eye a mutually convenient next-gen fighter deal.

item.title: CIA Director Ratcliffe's Surprise Moscow Trip Raises Questions Over Russia, Ukraine, Iran
item.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced visit to Moscow on August 25, US officials confirmed to RFE/RL, a rare trip that comes as Washington’s efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine have stalled and tensions over Moscow’s relationship with Iran have intensified. CIA Director Ratcliffe's Surprise Moscow Trip Raises Questions Over Russia, Ukraine, Iran.

item.title: Aggressive Recruiters Are Rounding Up Russians To Fight In Ukraine. In One Town, They're Pushing
item.description: Volunteers in the Penza region town of Bashmakovo have formed patrols to prevent military recruiters from taking local men to fight in Ukraine, an unusual grassroots response to the Russian state’s increasingly aggressive efforts to find troops for the war Aggressive Recruiters Are Rounding Up Russians To Fight In Ukraine. In One Town, They're Pushing.
